surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Ovechkin ties Bäckström for the Capitals’ assists record
paras: Matt Roy got the scoring started for the Capitals just 35 seconds into the game. The Caps went just over 21 minutes without a shot on goal, from early in the second to early in the third, while the Senators put 13 on net. Most teams don’t go that long without a shot even once a season. Ridly Greig and Hayden Hodgson scored just under five minutes apart midway through the second to turn a 1-0 deficit into a 2-1 lead. Pierre-Luc Dubois tied it 2-2 for Washington with less than eight minutes left. Cole Hutson won it a little over a minute into overtime.

The Capitals were outshot 27-17, but their looks were better, and the chances came out about even. Logan Thompson made 25 saves for the Capitals, and Samuel Ersson stopped 14 of 17 at the other end. By our Swing measure, Michael Amadio had the best night of anyone, even in a loss and with Hutson’s overtime winner in the game. The Capitals moved to 10-6-0, fourth in the Metropolitan, while the Senators dropped to 11-6-2, fourth in the Atlantic.
